sequence.selection: hash-ranked documents and one hash-ranked focus per document/group, before screenability or scoring; no replacement of unsupported rows
sequence.window: before + original + after; spacing and literal_tail are overlapping metadata and are never appended
sequence.trim: at a full 96-character left or 64-character right clip beginning/ending inside letters, remove only that outer letter fragment; preserve focus and adjacent whitespace/punctuation
sequence.keyboard: US/RU key pairs including Shift; natural script changes and focus first-letter layout are explicit user switches; subsequent glyphs follow the live backend group
sequence.intervention: Type leading focus nonletters in intended layouts; explicitly select the intended or opposite layout immediately before the first letter of the declared US/RU group. Wrong mode must produce a different observed glyph at that letter. Nonletter-only focus has no wrong intervention.
sequence.punctuation: physical keys chosen in intended layout, including ambiguous literal signs; no extra terminator or synthetic idle correction

settings_modes.early_off: context assist; early switch, learning, history, field reading and manual-layout cooldown disabled; context tracking enabled; 50 ms before every key-down, 30 ms before every key-up, engine timer callbacks after every key, 1.7 s idle with timer callbacks after every completed word, exactly as in the default mode, so the completed-word decision reaches a document that ends without a boundary key
settings_modes.default: application defaults with the early switch enabled explicitly, the configuration a user gets by turning that feature on: early switch from four letters, pause correction after 1.5 s, manual-layout protection, learning, context assist without field reading; 50 ms before every key-down, 30 ms before every key-up, engine timer callbacks after every key, 1.7 s idle with timer callbacks after every completed word; a layout selection is a manual switch only when it changes the live backend group

sequence.models: candidate and baseline context and prefix artifacts are injected explicitly; installed context and prefix bytes are never loaded; boundary, orthotactic and intent models are the pinned packaged files

default: candidate_context_baseline_prefix: ablation, reported but not gated

sequence.acceptance: every gate must hold for the candidate pair against the baseline pair in both settings modes and both lexical profiles
sequence.identifier_lexicon: src/keyswitch/resources/identifiers.json is lexical evidence for both readings of a token in the engine, the trainer and this replay alike; technical holdout rows therefore measure commands present in the shipped index, and behaviour on identifiers outside it is reported by a separate lexicon-blind development diagnostic
sequence.restoration_gate: net outcome: candidate exactly_restored minus correct_text_corruptions must reach the baseline pair's exactly_restored minus correct_text_corruptions, and the candidate must not corrupt more correct rows than that pair; the model decides what to convert, and it is judged by the balance rather than by a ban on ever being wrong
sequence.scope: in-process EditorBackend integration; no IME, native key loss, real focus races, actual injection acknowledgement, Enter/Tab submission or OS E2E proof; natural KEEP labels are not reviewed keyboard-intent ground truth

The editor opens in the layout of the first letter, the declared layout for the correct plan and the opposite layout for the wrong plan, and the first key carries no layout selection, so a wrong first letter has no manual choice behind it; a later key selects a layout only at a natural script change or at a glyph only the other layout has, as in protocol 4. Rows whose focus does not start with such a letter get no first plans and are listed in the selection as first_ineligible

sequence.correction_kind: every correction records the mode of the engine plan that made it (early, early_undo, boundary, pause, context_word, context_phrase, case, sign, symbols, undo, late_stroke, mention_shown, mention_hidden, ...); the replay idles 1.7 s after every word and the pause correction fires after 1.5 s, so a pause correction comes at a word's last letter like an early switch at its last letter: the kind, not the key, tells them apart
sequence.earliness: per pair in the default mode, over the wrong first plans: K is the key serial of the first correction whose target is the declared layout (the first key is serial 1, so K is the number of keys typed when it came) and L the letters of the focus word, its alphabetic run from the start; classes inside_word (K < L), last_letter (K = L), boundary_key (K = L + 1), later (K > L + 1) and never (no such correction). first_word_correct: the final text up to its first whitespace equals the expected text up to its first whitespace. started_right_ended_wrong: the first correction into the declared layout is of kind early and came at a key <= L (K < L + 1), and the first word is not correct (a right early switch undone later, for instance by the context model at the boundary). switch_key_sum and switch_key_rows: the sum and the count of K over the rows whose first word is correct (their mean K), switch_key_histogram their K in bins 1 to 8 and 9+; first_correction_kinds: the kind of the correction that gives K. False early switches, over the correct plans, each read against the layout of its row (its declared group): a false early switch is a correction of kind early whose target layout is not the row's layout; an early correction whose target is the row's layout brings the text back after another layer switched it away, and is a return, counted apart and never a false switch; a protocol-4 row with no declared layout has none to return to, so every early correction of it goes away. correct_first_plans (the correct first plans): false_early, the rows with at least one false early switch; false_early_on_focus, of those the rows whose first false early switch came at a key <= L; false_early_flicker, of those the rows whose final text is exact (the switch was undone); false_early_corrupted, of those the rows whose final text is not exact; early_returns, the rows with an early correction into the row's layout. correct_sequence_plans (the correct protocol-4 plans of the default mode): the same counts but false_early_on_focus, which a protocol-4 plan cannot say since it does not know the letters of its focus word. These counters are reported and never gated
sequence.acceptance: every gate must hold for the candidate pair against the baseline pair in both settings modes and both lexical profiles, on the protocol-4 plans and on the first plans of the default mode
sequence.identifier_lexicon: resources/identifiers.json is lexical evidence for both readings of a token in the engine, the trainer and this replay alike; technical holdout rows therefore measure commands present in the shipped index, and behaviour on identifiers outside it is reported by a separate lexicon-blind development diagnostic
sequence.restoration_gate: net outcome: candidate exactly_restored minus correct_text_corruptions must reach the baseline pair's exactly_restored minus correct_text_corruptions, and the candidate must not corrupt more correct rows than that pair; the model decides what to convert, and it is judged by the balance rather than by a ban on ever being wrong
sequence.first_gates: on the first plans of the default mode, candidate against baseline: net_restorations_at_least_baseline (exactly_restored minus correct_text_corruptions at least the baseline pair's), correct_text_preserved (no more corruptions than the baseline pair) and length_preserved (no length mismatch); the protocol-4 plans keep every gate of protocol 4, the sensor of false early switches inside a text
sequence.receipt_floor: the release receipt's restoration floor takes the default mode's margin from the first plans: the candidate pair restores at least as many first plans exactly as the baseline pair; early_off keeps its margin of one row and its share of 0.97 restored
sequence.scope: in-process EditorBackend integration; no IME, native key loss, real focus races, actual injection acknowledgement, Enter/Tab submission or OS E2E proof; natural KEEP labels are not reviewed keyboard-intent ground truth
